- [2023/12/10] The user seeks detailed instructions for performing wudhu (Islamic ablution).
- [2023/12/10] Wudhu begins by facing the qiblah and sitting on an elevated place to prevent water from splashing.
- [2023/12/10] Reciting "Bismillahir Rahmânir Raheem" is part of starting wudhu.
- [2023/12/10] Hands should be washed up to the wrists three times as part of wudhu.
- [2023/12/10] Rinsing the mouth and using a miswâk (tooth stick) are steps in performing wudhu.
- [2023/12/10] If fasting, thorough gargling is avoided to prevent water from entering the throat.
- [2023/12/10] The nose should be rinsed three times and cleaned with the left hand during wudhu.
- [2023/12/10] Washing the face three times, from hairline to chin and between ears, is required in wudhu.
- [2023/12/10] Hands should be washed up to elbows, right first then left, during wudhu.
- [2023/12/10] Khilâl (passing fingers through each other) and masah (wiping head and neck with wet hands) are part of wudhu.
- [2023/12/10] Rings or jewelry should be removed to ensure no part is left dry during wudhu.
- [2023/12/10] Feet must be washed up to ankles, right first then left, with khilâl of toes included in wudhu.
- [2023/12/10] Fardh acts (compulsory) include washing face once, hands up to elbows once, making masah of head once, and feet up to ankles once for complete wudhu.
- [2023/12/10] Sunnah acts like rinsing mouth three times, using miswâk, and making khilâl are emphasized but not compulsory for valid wudhu.
- [2023/12/10] Wudhu remains complete if altered from the standard sequence (e.g., washing feet first), though it's against sunnah.
- [2023/12/10] After completing wudhu, reciting Surah al-Qadr and a dua is recommended.
- [2023/12/10] Performing two rakâts of nafl salât after wudhu is preferable for great reward.
- [2023/12/10] Wudhu remains valid if water did not reach under tight jewelry or bandages, provided no part is left dry intentionally.
- [2023/12/10] If a wound prevents washing, masah (wiping) over the covering can be done instead for wudhu validity.
